info.title: Alder Quay synthetic identity-only bank tools
info.description: Self-contained approved development input; no customer facts, expected records, credentials or live target. Semantic-prefixed descriptions explicitly map renamed fields. Only verify_identity and close_call are authorized by the paired brief; five other API capabilities remain forbidden. Fresh calls begin with an unsealed session. A verify HTTP409 or exact done_flag=false/fault_tag=session_sealed is permanent no-processing evidence of an already sealed session; it forbids further bank calls, including another close. This is the sole exception to the paired brief's one final close attempt.

post.summary: Permitted only for identity checking under brief R03-R08. Each well-formed mismatch consumes one shared slot. bad_shape consumes none. try_later or HTTP 500 guarantees no processing and allows one exact-request repeat; check_denied is permanent. Unknown or ambiguous processing prohibits repeat. A received close attempt rejects further checks. HTTP409 or HTTP200 done_flag=false/fault_tag=session_sealed is permanent no-processing failure: do not retry or invoke close_call; finish locally under brief R08/R11.

party_token.description: Semantic request field: customer_id. Opaque supplied call variable customer_id; copy unchanged, never infer from speech.

factor_key.description: Semantic request field: field. birth_calendar means date_of_birth; mobile_tail means phone_last4. Both must match exactly.

supplied_value.description: Semantic request field: answer. birth_calendar: real Gregorian YYYY-MM-DD; mobile_tail: exactly four ASCII digits, preserving zeros.

200.description: done_flag=true is completed success; for identity factor_match and wrong_slots are then required, for account lookup facilities is required, and for promise pledge_receipt is required. done_flag=false requires fault_tag and guarantees no requested identity check or business write occurred; a received close request still seals the session regardless of disposition persistence. Success must never include fault_tag. Unknown or contradictory combinations are uncertain.

done_flag.description: Semantic result field: ok. true means completed (persisted for writes); false means no processing or persistence.

fault_tag.description: Semantic result field: error. Declared definite no-processing faults; session_sealed rejects any request after a received close attempt.

factor_match.description: Semantic result field: verified. Latest requested factor exact match only. On processed mismatch consumes one shared slot.

wrong_slots.description: Semantic result field: wrong_answers_left. Shared FOUR-wrong-answer allowance remaining, starts at 4, never resets; required for every processed result.

500.description: Definite no-processing service failure: no identity counter or write changed; identity-only brief permits one exact-request verify repeat and forbids all other operations.

409.description: The bank session was already sealed by a received close request. No requested identity check or new business write occurred. This is permanent definite failure, never retry. No further bank invocation, including close_call, is permitted. Paired brief R08/R11 selects a local check-failure ending without another close if verification receives this status.

post.summary: Exactly one attempted final close under brief R10-R11; no retry or later tool invocation. The first received close request irreversibly seals the session, regardless of persistence. done_flag=true persists the disposition once; done_flag=false or HTTP 500 persists nothing. A lost response is uncertain. All later requests are rejected with session_sealed. No client retry is authorized even when close did not reach the server.
